messages:
jamie: Heads-up: deploy-bot queued a deploy for checkout-service tonight 22:00 UTC. PR includes a DB migration that adds a nullable `payment_method` column. Question: do we treat this as a patch (v1.2.x) or bump minor?

sasha: If the migration is additive + nullable and consumers don't rely on the new column, semver-wise it's a patch. But callers might enable logic later — release notes should call it out.

leo: Agree patch. Only reason to minor-bump is if we ship behavior changes that are visible without opt-in. Adding a nullable column is backwards compatible.

ana: Quick nit — our deploy-bot currently auto-bumps patch for PRs flagged "non-breaking". Who flagged this one?

jamie: I did. I selected "non-breaking" when triggering the release. deploy-bot showed `v1.2.3 -> v1.2.4 (patch)` in the UI.

chris: I'd rather we standardize tagging for any migration: tag still follows semver but add buildmeta to tag name for traceability, e.g. `v1.2.4+db.3467890123` or `v1.2.4+mig.20260320`. keeps semver precedence unchanged while giving context.

sasha: Leaning no on buildmeta in git tag names — it fragments what we search for. Could put that metadata in release notes or annotated tag message instead.

leo: Also recall buildmeta (`+`) is ignored for precedence so it's safe semver-wise, but tooling sometimes strips `+` and CI jobs fail. I vote for `v1.2.4` tag and an annotated tag message with `Migration: add payment_method (nullable) — PR #4321 — commit abcdef1`

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: release created: checkout-service@v1.2.4 (patch) by jamie. canary window 22:00-23:00 UTC. rollback-policy: app-only rollback allowed; DB rollback requires manual coordination.

ana: Important: add a rollback plan to the release notes. Since migration is additive and nullable, app rollback should be safe; still include the SQL to drop column and a checklist if we need to revert.

jamie: SQL snippet to include in notes:
```sql
-- safe reverse if no consumers populated the column
ALTER TABLE checkout DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS payment_method;
```

chris: Also add a monitoring checklist — slow writes, index bloat, column cardinality. If any signal trips, we prefer app rollback and feature flag off.

leo: One more deploy-bot policy debate — should deploy-bot auto-promote to minor if PR touches `migrations/` and includes destructive DDL (drop/rename)? Right now it only looks at the "breaking-change:" marker in PR body.

sasha: We should update the heuristics: scan migration files for keywords `DROP`, `RENAME`, `ALTER ... TYPE` and flag as "potentially breaking" and require human confirm.

jamie: Good call. For tonight let's proceed as patch, tag `v1.2.4`, add annotated tag message with PR + migration details, include the SQL rollback snippet in release notes, and add monitoring checklist. I'll also open a small RFC to change deploy-bot heuristics for migration scanning.

ana: Can someone add the rollback snippet & monitoring checklist to the release notes before canary kickoff?

chris: I'll do it and @jamie please add the annotated tag.

jamie: Will do. Also filing a follow-up ticket to add the migration-scan rule to deploy-bot: infra#789.

leo: Thanks — marking this resolved for the release channel. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: reminder scheduled: canary starts in 10m for checkout-service@v1.2.4. Logs will be forwarded to #incidents if error-rate > 2%

sasha: Thanks everyone — please ping if anything unexpected during canary.

chris: If we hit an issue, rollback plan: 1) roll app to v1.2.3 2) monitor 3) if data shows schema problems, open emergency migration reversal with DB team.

jamie: Posted release notes and annotated tag. Canary green so far. Will update if any anomalies.
